newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end lower after record run.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end lower after record run.

text.p: Swiss shares closed lower a day after a record run on Tuesday amid insecurity about near-term developments on Wall Street.
"There is a lot of nervousness because of New York", one dealer said, adding that investors were reluctant to take positions as long as a correction on Wall Street seemed to continue.
The firmer undertone in the U.S. dollar and rising Swiss bond futures gave the market some support, a trader noted.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) lost 13.9 points, or 0.35 percent, to end at 3,910.6.
All-share SPI was down 8.85 points to 2,495.61.
UBS, which lagged behind the market on Tuesday, stood out among blue chips. The bearer shares jumped 13 francs, or 1.09 percent, to 1,212.
On the other hand, some of Tuesday's top performers were among the biggest loosers. CS Holding slumped 1.27 percent to 136.50. Nestle and Zurich gave up 0.77 percent and 1.06 percent, respectively.
Surveillance profited from the firming U.S. dollar, adding 15 francs to 3,085.
Watchmaker SMH's registered shares were slightly higher, while SMH bearer shares eased. SMH chairman Nicolas Hayek on Tuesday predicted a rise in profit and sales in 1996.
Roche, which led the actives list, fell 20 francs to 10,130 after touching an all-time high at 10,175. Ciba registered shares were flat at 1,624. Sandoz fell three francs to 1,528.

Among second-tier shares, bourse newcomer Elma Electronics, a former Sulzer unit that was spun off, soared to 295 francs on its first day of trading after being priced at 275 in the initial public offering.
